engineering: Verify behavior through public seams and keep tests deterministic and offline.
Prefer the smallest change that satisfies the approved Ticket and preserves existing contracts.
Do not hide failures by weakening assertions, swallowing errors, or skipping required gates.
workflow: Work only in the assigned isolated worktree and within the approved Ticket scope.
Treat the orchestrator as the only lifecycle authority; the supervisor may propose dispatch and post-approval merge commands, but only the orchestrator validates and applies them.
Ticket roles report through Handoff Receipts and do not assign work or message one another directly.
Report unresolved risk explicitly in the Handoff Receipt.
repository: Do not rewrite shared history, force-push, delete branches, or change repository visibility.
Do not commit .factory runtime state, prompts, logs, credentials, or Evidence Packets automatically.
Preserve QA-owned protected Acceptance Tests and repository-defined verification commands.
